## Summary

MiniMax-M3 BF16 proxy pretraining on MI455X (gfx1250) with the Megatron backend, on Megatron-LM core_v0.19.2.

- **gfx1250 MSA kernels.** Wave32 WMMA versions of the FlyDSL MSA forward, backward (dQ, dK/dV) and the indexer's block max (`minimax_m3/flydsl/msa_w32.py`, `msa_token_fwd_w32.py`, `msa_token_bwd_w32.py`, and a wave32 builder in `index_block_max.py`). The originals use MFMA, `permlane32` and `ds_read_tr16`, which gfx1250 does not have, and failed at compile with `Cannot select: permlane32.swap`. gfx950 keeps the MFMA kernels; only the dispatch changed.
- **Megatron-core 0.19.** `MinimaxSparseAttention` takes the `name=` that 0.19's `TransformerLayer` passes, and the fused Adam clip patch takes 0.19's `group=` in its reduce-max and reads `get_grads_for_grad_norm`. Without these, building an M3 model and the first optimizer step raise a `TypeError` on this base.
- **Fused Adam clip patch builds again.** No hard-coded `-std=c++17`: torch 2.14's headers need C++20, and the patch logged the build error and training ran without it.
- **`megatron.optimizer.te_l2norm_large_tensor` patch.** TE's `multi_tensor_l2norm` reads out of bounds when a multi-tensor call has a tensor of 2^31 or more elements. The Primus-Turbo grouped GEMM keeps a layer's experts in one weight (4.8e9 elements on one GPU), so the first step faulted or ran with a wrong grad norm. The patch splits such tensors into 2^30-element views for the norm.
- **Example.** `examples/megatron/configs/MI455X/minimax_m3-BF16-pretrain.yaml`, `examples/megatron/models/minimax-m3/run_minimax_m3_mi455x.sh` and its README. Defaults: Primus's HIP fused Adam with in-kernel clipping and BF16 writeback, no per-step NaN check. The four-GPU baseline is EP4 with 8 layers and GBS 32 (8 micro-batches per rank, as in the MI355X 8-layer config).

## Results

4x MI455X (`ctheliosr-rck-g02-e15-01`), `amdprimus/amdprimus:tas-20261019`, 4-layer proxy (3 dense + 1 MSA/MoE layer), seq 4096, MBS 1, mock data, 10 iterations, on `dev/mi455x_v3` c19456f1.

| GPUs | Layers | ms/iter | Tokens/s/GPU | TFLOP/s/GPU | Memory/GPU | lm loss, iteration 10 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 142.4 | 28,757 | 474.4 | 237.7 GB | 10.98864 |
| 2 (EP2) | 4 | 130.1 | 31,493 | 519.7 | 177.9 GB | 10.31194 |
| 4 (EP4) | 4 | 121.6 | 33,684 | 555.8 | 147.3 GB | 9.66907 |
| 4 (EP4) | 8 | 254.9 | 16,068 | 426.1 | 280.0 GB | 9.11894 |

On the same node, the previous base (Megatron-LM d3528a21) ran at the same speed (142.3, 130.5, 121.9 and 255.5 ms) with the same losses, and used 4–9 GB more memory per GPU. Primus's Triton AdamW (`PRIMUS_FUSED_ADAM_CLIP=0`) is 10% slower than the HIP fused Adam on one GPU and 6.5% slower on EP2, so the default stays `PRIMUS_FUSED_ADAM_CLIP=1`.

The baseline, EP4 with 8 layers, on `ctheliosr-rck-g02-e15-02` (compare within one node):

| Layers | MBS / GBS | ms/iter | Tokens/s/GPU | TFLOP/s/GPU | Memory/GPU | lm loss, iteration 10 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 (baseline) | 1 / 32 | 1536.6 | 21,325 | 565.5 | 280.2 GB | 8.19595 |
| 8 | 1 / 4 | 247.6 | 16,545 | 438.8 | 280.2 GB | 9.11894 |
| 4 | 1 / 32 | 736.3 | 44,504 | 734.0 | 147.5 GB | 9.24521 |

The baseline repeated at 1538.2 ms with the same loss.

## Test plan

- [x] gfx1250, on c19456f1: `tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_minimax_m3_*.py`, `test_fused_adam_clip_patches.py`, `test_l2norm_large_tensor_patches.py`: 131 passed
- [x] gfx1250, on c19456f1: 1 GPU, EP2, EP4 with 4 and 8 layers: 10 iterations, 0 NaN, losses identical to the previous base on the same node
- [x] gfx1250, on this branch merged into `dev/mi455x_v3` db5fe1fd: the tests above plus `patches/test_topk_router_patches.py`, 139 passed; 1 GPU on `ctheliosr-rck-g02-e15-02`, 132.3 ms/iter, loss 10.98864, 0 NaN
- [x] gfx1250, 91eea9f3 on `ctheliosr-rck-g02-e15-02`: EP4 with 8 layers at GBS 32 (twice) and 4, and 4 layers at GBS 32: 10 iterations, 0 NaN
- [x] gfx1250, 654da6d0's launcher (options removed), 1 GPU: 10 iterations, 0 NaN, fused Adam patch enabled
- [x] `pre-commit` on the changed files, `tools/ci/check_version_consistency.py`
- [ ] gfx950 (`ci:gpu`): the MFMA kernels were not run here; only their dispatch changed

Jira: [LWPARCH-552](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/LWPARCH-552)

#### 2. 🟠 Should fix: Single-optimizer runs clip MTP params with the main-model norm: this PR adds the MTP guard only to the chained path
`primus/backends/megatron/patches/te_patches/fused_adam_clip_patches.py:616`

The new MTP separate-grad-norm-group guard exists only in `_chained_step_with_device_clip`. With a single optimizer, `MegatronOptimizer.step` calls `patched_clip_grad_norm`, which computes the main norm (MTP excluded by Megatron's getter) and lets FusedAdam clip every param, MTP included, with it. Megatron-core 0.19 instead clips MTP params with their own group norm, and nothing raises here. Add the `has_grad_norm_group` check to `patched_clip_grad_norm`. The skip-threshold part does not apply: in 0.19 only `ChainedOptimizer.step` honours `grad_norm_skip_threshold`.

**Who is affected:** Users who set `PRIMUS_FUSED_ADAM_CLIP=1` with MTP enabled on a model whose optimizer is not chained (for example, a dense model with one model chunk).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

<details><summary>Nits and less certain findings (19)</summary>

**6. Wave32 forward host wrapper duplicates `msa_token_fwd` input checks and launch logic** (`primus/backends/megatron/core/transformer/minimax_m3/flydsl/msa_token_fwd_w32.py:336`)

`msa_token_fwd_wave32` repeats most of `msa_token_fwd`'s host wrapper: the asserts, the `softmax_scale` default, `.contiguous()`, the allocations, `check_buffer_bytes`, and the cache/compile/launch steps. The two are not identical: the wave32 wrapper defaults `remap` to `lpt`, has no `waves` clamping, and uses a different cache key. Sharing the input checks, as `msa_token_bwd` does by choosing the builder inside one wrapper, would keep them from drifting.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers changing the MSA forward input contract; no runtime effect.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**7. Large non-contiguous grads may be fully copied during norm via `reshape(-1)`** (`primus/backends/megatron/patches/te_patches/l2norm_large_tensor_patches.py:36`)

`_pieces` uses `tensor.reshape(-1).split()`, which for a non-contiguous tensor above 2^30 elements materialises a full copy (~19 GB for the 4.8e9-element fp32 expert grad) and can OOM. A transposed-tensor test confirmed no shared storage. Use `view(-1)` or leave non-contiguous tensors whole; also note that `per_tensor=True` leaves the OOB fault reachable and the docstring is inaccurate.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: Grads passed to `get_grad_norm_fp32` are `main_grad` views from `param_and_grad_buffer._get` (`grad_data[start:end].view(shape)`, always contiguous), and TE's `multi_tensor_l2norm` binding is documented as taking contiguous tensors. All Megatron callers (`clip_grads.py`, `training/utils.py`) pass `per_tensor=False`, so the unsplit `per_tensor=True` path is not reached._

**8. Broken l2norm patch installation would pass tests: this PR only tests the wrapper function** (`tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_l2norm_large_tensor_patches.py:1`)

The tests only exercise `split_large_tensors` with a fake l2norm. Nothing checks that `patch_te_l2norm_large_tensor` rebinds `clip_grads.l2_norm_impl`, that `get_grad_norm_fp32`/`_get_grad_norm_tensor` pick it up, idempotency, `multi_tensor_l2norm` rebinding, or `noop_flag`/`chunk_size` forwarding. Add tests for the install path.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers relying on CI to catch a regression in how the l2norm large-tensor patch is installed into Megatron's `clip_grads`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**9. gfx1250 forward silently drops most tuning knobs: this PR forwards `**config` to a wave32 path reading only `remap`** (`primus/backends/megatron/core/transformer/minimax_m3/flydsl/msa_token_fwd.py:788`)

On gfx1250, `msa_token_fwd` returns early into `msa_token_fwd_wave32(..., **config)`, which reads only `remap` from `config`. So `step_keys`, `k_via_lds`, `pipeline`, `barriers` and `waves` are silently ignored, while its docstring says only `waves` is ignored. In `test_every_tuning_path_matches_eager`, now enabled on gfx1250, three of the four knob variants therefore build the same kernel; only `remap="block"` differs. Document or reject the unsupported knobs, or skip those variants on gfx1250. Both paths default to `remap="lpt"` (`build_fwd`'s default), so there is no default mismatch.

**Who is affected:** Only callers or tests on gfx1250 (MI455X) that pass forward tuning knobs; the production caller `msa_function.py` passes none.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**10. gfx1250 arch dispatch repeated as bare substring checks at five entry points** (`primus/backends/megatron/core/transformer/minimax_m3/flydsl/msa_token_bwd.py:1096`)

The arch dispatch `"gfx1250" in get_hip_arch()` is repeated at five sites (`msa_token_fwd.py`, `msa_token_bwd.py` x2, `index_block_max.py` x2). Only `msa_token_fwd` queries it on every call; the bwd/index sites check it only when the kernel cache misses. The function-local imports there load the w32 builder modules, not `get_hip_arch`. Leaving the arch out of the cache keys is harmless because the arch does not change within a process. Consider one shared helper (e.g. in `msa_w32.py`, or reuse `_is_gfx1250()`); an explicit unsupported-arch error would be a nice extra, but other archs already failed opaquely on the base.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers of the MiniMax-M3 flydsl kernels; no runtime impact on gfx950/gfx1250.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**11. CI never runs the new gfx1250 wave32 kernels: this PR adds no dispatch or CI-runnable tests** (`tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_minimax_m3_flydsl_fwd.py:29`)

The new gfx1250 wave32 kernels (`msa_token_fwd_w32`, `msa_token_bwd_w32`, the w32 `index_block_max` builders, the `msa_w32` helpers) are covered only by widening the existing gfx950 numerical tests to gfx1250. On a gfx1250 GPU those tests do exercise the w32 path, since dispatch follows the arch. No test asserts which path was taken, and the CI runners are gfx942/gfx950, so the w32 kernels never run in CI.

**Who is affected:** Regressions in the gfx1250 w32 kernels go unnoticed unless someone runs the suite on MI455X by hand.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**12. Test `_build` hard-codes `add_bias_linear=False`, possibly dropping bias coverage and breaking overrides** (`tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_minimax_m3_msa.py:458`)

The shared `_build` helper hard-codes `add_bias_linear=False` on every arch to work around a gfx1250 hipBLASLt gap, losing bias coverage elsewhere. Passing it beside `**overrides` makes `_build(add_bias_linear=...)` raise a 'multiple values for keyword argument' TypeError. Gate it on gfx1250 or use `overrides.setdefault`.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: The value mirrors the model's only preset, `minimax_m3.yaml:138` (`add_bias_linear: false`), and the inline comment documents the gfx1250 reason, so it is a deliberate choice that tests the configuration M3 actually runs. None of the ten `_build` callers passes `add_bias_linear`, so the duplicate-keyword `TypeError` cannot occur today._

**13. Dropped or mangled `name` forwarding would pass the module-name test: it only checks finite output** (`tests/unit_tests/backends/megatron/test_minimax_m3_msa.py:491`)

`test_builds_with_the_module_name` constructs `MinimaxSparseAttention` directly with a non-None `name`. That covers the new `name` parameter and the conditional `**({"name": name})` forwarding, which on the base raised a `TypeError`. It goes around `TransformerLayer`/`build_module`, though, and asserts only finite output, not that `name` reached the parent `SelfAttention`. No version gate is needed: the pinned Megatron-core is 0.19, whose `SelfAttention` accepts `name`. Consider asserting on the forwarded name or building through the layer spec.

**Who is affected:** Only test coverage for the MiniMax-M3 MSA module; runtime users are not affected.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**14. Running the MI455X YAML with only `PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH=8192` aborts: this PR hard-codes `max_position_embeddings` 4096** (`examples/megatron/configs/MI455X/minimax_m3-BF16-pretrain.yaml:48`)

`max_position_embeddings` defaults to a hard-coded 4096 instead of `${PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH}`, although the comment says to leave it at `seq_length`. Running this YAML without the launcher and setting only `PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH=8192` makes Megatron's `validate_args` assert `max_position_embeddings >= seq_length` at startup. The same applies to `num_layers` versus the `PRIMUS_LAYER_FREQ` lists when only `PRIMUS_TOTAL_LAYERS` is overridden. The launcher derives all of these together, and the header says to launch through it. `mock_data` and forced load balancing can be overridden on the CLI (the launcher passes `--mock_data` and `"$@"`).

**Who is affected:** Users who run the MI455X YAML directly through primus-cli instead of `run_minimax_m3_mi455x.sh` and override only the sequence length or layer count.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**15. Hipify output written into the package tree may fail on read-only installs** (`.gitignore:42`)

The extension build writes `fused_adam_clip_kernel.hip` next to the `.cu` inside the package, hidden by `.gitignore`. This fails on read-only/site-packages installs and can race when several ranks JIT-build at once. Build into a cache or build directory instead.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: I compared `_load_extension` in repo/ and head/: both pass `Path(__file__).with_name('fused_adam_clip_kernel.cu')` to `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`, so the in-tree hipify output predates this PR. I did not check the race claim in torch's source; my understanding, unverified here, is that hipify runs under the build directory's `FileBaton`, which would serialise ranks on one node._

**Related past reviews:** [#864](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/864) on `.gitignore`

**16. Argmax tie-break `pick` helper duplicated between gfx950 and gfx1250 indexer kernels** (`primus/backends/megatron/core/transformer/minimax_m3/flydsl/index_block_max.py:160`)

`_build_index_block_max_w32` redefines `pick(v1, a1, v2, a2)` identically to the one in `build_index_block_max`. The tie-break must stay identical across gfx950 and gfx1250 for outputs to agree. Hoist it to one module-level helper.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers editing the indexer tie-break; gfx1250 (`_build_index_block_max_w32`) and gfx950 (`build_index_block_max`) paths could drift apart.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**17. Megatron-core 0.19 grad-norm getter rename probed independently at class and instance level** (`primus/backends/megatron/patches/te_patches/fused_adam_clip_patches.py:81`)

The Megatron-core 0.19 rename (`get_main_grads_for_grad_norm` -> `get_grads_for_grad_norm`) is detected twice. `_install_patch` uses `hasattr(MegatronOptimizer, ...)` to choose which name to patch, and `_grads_for_grad_norm` uses `getattr(optimizer, ...)` on the instance. With stock Megatron both resolve to the same name, because subclasses inherit the base-class method. They would diverge only if a subclass defined the new name while the base class lacked it. Computing the name once would remove that hypothetical split.

**Who is affected:** No current configuration; only a future or custom optimizer subclass that defines only one of the two names.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**18. Wave32 modules redefine `_LOG2E`, `TK`, `KS`, `DT`, `STRIDE` instead of importing them** (`primus/backends/megatron/core/transformer/minimax_m3/flydsl/msa_token_fwd_w32.py:52`)

`msa_token_fwd_w32.py:52-57` redefines `_LOG2E`, `TK`, `KS`, `DT`, `STRIDE` identical to `msa_token_fwd.py`, though it already imports other constants from there and `msa_token_bwd_w32.py` imports `TK`/`KS`/`STRIDE`. Same for `_LOG2E`/`DT` in `msa_token_bwd_w32.py:45-46`. Import them to avoid drift.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers editing the MSA wave32 kernels' tile geometry.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**19. Backend-wide Megatron-core 0.19 fused-Adam rework is possibly bundled into the gfx1250 port** (`primus/backends/megatron/patches/te_patches/fused_adam_clip_patches.py:81`)

Besides the MiniMax-M3 gfx1250 port, the PR carries a backend-wide Megatron-core 0.19 compatibility rework of the fused Adam clip patch (getter rename, `grad_norm_group`, MTP rejection, skip threshold, `group=` reduce, dropping `-std=c++17`). Every hunk there references 0.19/torch 2.14, not gfx1250. Consider splitting it into its own PR.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: `git ls-tree` at the base shows third_party/Megatron-LM at 4b4acac9 (core_v0.19.2, c19456f #1321), while the patch dates from #1219 against the older getter name. run_minimax_m3_mi455x.sh:64 enables PRIMUS_FUSED_ADAM_CLIP by default and the README benchmarks on c19456f with that patch enabled._

**20. Per-head row index recomputed four times in wave32 forward kernel** (`primus/backends/megatron/core/transformer/minimax_m3/flydsl/msa_token_fwd_w32.py:284`)

`(tok * Bn + b) * fx.Index(Hq) + head` is computed as `head_row` at line 196 but rebuilt for `q_row` (167), `o_row` (284) and the LSE offset (303). Define `head_row` first and reuse it for all four offsets.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers of the gfx1250 forward kernel; no runtime impact.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**21. Patched getter names still say `get_main_grads` while wrapping `get_grads_for_grad_norm`** (`primus/backends/megatron/patches/te_patches/fused_adam_clip_patches.py:583`)

`original_get_main_grads` and `patched_get_main_grads_for_grad_norm` now wrap `get_grads_for_grad_norm` on Megatron-core 0.19+ via `setattr(MegatronOptimizer, grads_for_norm_name, ...)`. Rename them neutrally (e.g. `original_grads_for_norm`) to match `grads_for_norm_name`.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers reading the fused Adam clip patch on Megatron-core with `get_grads_for_grad_norm`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**22. Default MI455X example runs ~4% slower with 8 GB more memory: turbo attention left off** (`examples/megatron/configs/MI455X/minimax_m3-BF16-pretrain.yaml:134`)

`use_turbo_attention: false` in the YAML and `USE_TURBO_ATTENTION=False` in the launcher, yet the README measures `USE_TURBO_ATTENTION=True` at 151.3 vs 158.2 ms/iter and 233.8 vs 241.5 GB with equal loss. The only stated blocker (fmha_bwd failure) is already handled by the launcher's Triton backend fallback. Consider defaulting it to True.

**Who is affected:** Users running the MI455X MiniMax-M3 example with its defaults.

MiniMax-M3 BF16 proxy pretraining on MI455X (gfx1250) with the Megatron backend, on Megatron-LM core_v0.19.2.

- **gfx1250 MSA kernels.** Wave32 WMMA versions of the FlyDSL MSA forward, backward (dQ, dK/dV) and the indexer's block max (`minimax_m3/flydsl/msa_w32.py`, `msa_token_fwd_w32.py`, `msa_token_bwd_w32.py`, and a wave32 builder in `index_block_max.py`). The originals use MFMA, `permlane32` and `ds_read_tr16`, which gfx1250 does not have, and failed at compile with `Cannot select: permlane32.swap`. gfx950 keeps the MFMA kernels; only the dispatch changed.
- **Megatron-core 0.19.** `MinimaxSparseAttention` takes the `name=` that 0.19's `TransformerLayer` passes, and the fused Adam clip patch takes 0.19's `group=` in its reduce-max and reads `get_grads_for_grad_norm`. Without these, building an M3 model and the first optimizer step raise a `TypeError` on this base.
- **Fused Adam clip patch builds again.** No hard-coded `-std=c++17`: torch 2.14's headers need C++20, and the patch logged the build error and training ran without it.
- **`megatron.optimizer.te_l2norm_large_tensor` patch.** TE's `multi_tensor_l2norm` reads out of bounds when a multi-tensor call has a tensor of 2^31 or more elements. The Primus-Turbo grouped GEMM keeps a layer's experts in one weight (4.8e9 elements on one GPU), so the first step faulted or ran with a wrong grad norm. +# MiniMax-M3 proxy on MI455X
+
+MiniMax-M3 BF16 pretraining on MI455X (gfx1250), as a shallow proxy of the real 60-layer model: the
+first three layers stay dense, and every later layer is one MSA (MiniMax Sparse Attention) layer plus
+one MoE layer (128 experts, top-4, hidden 6144, 64 query / 4 KV heads of dim 128). The launcher's
+default is 4 layers on one GPU; the baseline is 8 layers on four GPUs (see Baseline). Sequence length
+4096, MBS 1, mock data, full recompute of the first layer. The config is
+`examples/megatron/configs/MI455X/minimax_m3-BF16-pretrain.yaml` and the launcher is
+`run_minimax_m3_mi455x.sh`: with `PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=container` (default) it starts a new container of
+`DOCKER_IMAGE` from the host and re-runs itself inside it; with `PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=direct` it runs inside
+the current container.
+
+MSA is not Primus-Turbo attention. `msa_backend=flydsl` (the default) runs the kernels under
+`primus/backends/megatron/core/transformer/minimax_m3/flydsl/`. On gfx950 those are the MFMA kernels.
+On gfx1250 they are the wave32 WMMA kernels (`*_w32.py`); a tree without that port fails at compile
+with `Cannot select: permlane32.swap`. `PRIMUS_MSA_BACKEND=eager` is the plain-PyTorch reference and
+does not need those kernels. The experts use Primus-Turbo's grouped GEMM and RMSNorm uses
+Primus-Turbo. DeepEP stays off (see Known issues).
+
+The default image is `amdprimus/amdprimus:tas-20261019` (see the DeepSeek-V3 example's README),
+`amdprimus/amdprimus@sha256:d653324d124e218f43c92eaac3cfc5d05059bd45fb4abf5bdfb78b987af4af87`: torch
+2.14.0 on ROCm 10.2.0a20261011, Triton 3.8.0, Transformer Engine 2.19.0.dev0 (bfe94fbe5),
+Primus-Turbo 0.6.1.dev2, FlyDSL 0.3.4.1 and AITER 0.1.24.post1. Every run below used that image and
+its own Primus-Turbo.

+## Run
+
+```bash
+# On the host, 1 GPU (the default: 4 layers, EP1, GBS 1). Pick a free device on a shared node.
+HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 bash examples/megatron/models/minimax-m3/run_minimax_m3_mi455x.sh
+
+# The baseline: 4 GPUs, 8 layers, EP4, GBS 32
+GPUS_PER_NODE=4 PRIMUS_TOTAL_LAYERS=8 GBS=32 bash examples/megatron/models/minimax-m3/run_minimax_m3_mi455x.sh

+PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=direct bash examples/megatron/models/minimax-m3/run_minimax_m3_mi455x.sh

+  here, 60 is the full model). The launcher keeps the first three layers dense and sets
+  `moe_layer_freq`, `sparse_attention_freq` and `sparse_disable_index_value` to the same length.

+  `--profile_ranks '[0,1,2,3]'` for every rank. `PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING` (default `1`): see

+  `PRIMUS_USER`, `PRIMUS_EXP_NAME`, which make up the output directory `<workspace>/<team>/<user>/<exp>`.

+The defaults are in the script. Arguments to the script are appended to the Primus command line, for
+example `--gradient_accumulation_fusion True`.

+**Output.** The console log is written to `output/<team>/<user>/<exp>/train.log`. From the host,
+training runs as root in the new container, so the files it creates are owned by root. Inside a

+  ``k = (lane // 16) * 16 + i`` for ``i`` in ``0..15``. One lane holds 16
+  contiguous K of one row; the two lane groups split K.
+* B, matrix_b so that ``C = A @ B``: ``col = lane % 16``,
+  ``k = (lane // 16) * 16 + i``. One lane holds 16 contiguous K of one column.
+* C, ``[16, 16]`` fp32: ``col = lane % 16``,
+  ``row = (lane // 16) * 8 + i`` for ``i`` in ``0..7``. Lanes ``0..15`` hold
+  rows ``0..7``, lanes ``16..31`` hold rows ``8..15``.
+

+    """One ``v_wmma_f32_16x16x32_bf16``. ``a``/``b`` are 16 bf16, ``c`` is 8 f32.

+"""Split tensors of more than 2^30 elements before Transformer Engine's l2norm.
+
+On ROCm, TE's ``multi_tensor_l2norm`` reads out of bounds when it is given more
+than one tensor and one of them has 2^31 or more elements: a memory fault in
+``custom_multi_tensor_l2norm_kernel``, or a wrong norm when the address happens
+to be mapped. A lone tensor of that size is fine. Seen with TE 2.19.0.dev0.
+
+Megatron passes every gradient to one l2norm call for the grad norm, and
+Primus-Turbo's grouped GEMM keeps all experts of a layer in one parameter, so
+for example MiniMax-M3's 128 experts of 6144 x 6144 (fc1) are 4.8e9 elements.
+The wrapper gives the kernel views of at most 2^30 elements instead; for the
+total norm (``per_tensor=False``) that is the same norm.
+"""
+
+from functools import wraps
+
+import torch
+
+from primus.backends.megatron.patches._patch_guard import is_patched, mark_patched
+from primus.backends.megatron.patches._rebind import rebind_everywhere
+from primus.core.patches import PatchContext, register_patch
+from primus.core.utils.module_utils import log_rank_0
+
+_PATCH_KEY = "megatron.optimizer.te_l2norm_large_tensor"
+_MAX_NUMEL = 1 << 30
+
+
+def _pieces(tensor: torch.Tensor):
+    if tensor.numel() <= _MAX_NUMEL:
+        return [tensor]
+    return list(tensor.reshape(-1).split(_MAX_NUMEL))
+
+
+def split_large_tensors(l2norm):
+    """``l2norm`` with every tensor of more than ``_MAX_NUMEL`` elements split into views."""
+
+    @wraps(l2norm)
+    def l2norm_split(chunk_size, noop_flag, tensor_lists, per_tensor=False):
+        if not per_tensor and any(t.numel() > _MAX_NUMEL for tensors in tensor_lists for t in tensors):
+            tensor_lists = [[p for t in tensors for p in _pieces(t)] for tensors in tensor_lists]
+        return l2norm(chunk_size, noop_flag, tensor_lists, per_tensor)
+
+    return l2norm_split
+
+
+@register_patch(
+    _PATCH_KEY,
+    backend="megatron",
+    phase="before_train",
+    description="Split tensors of more than 2^30 elements before TE multi_tensor_l2norm (grad norm)",
+)
+def patch_te_l2norm_large_tensor(ctx: PatchContext):
+    del ctx
+    from megatron.core.optimizer import clip_grads
+
+    if is_patched(clip_grads, _PATCH_KEY):
+        return
+    l2norm = split_large_tensors(clip_grads.l2_norm_impl)
+    rebound = rebind_everywhere(clip_grads, "l2_norm_impl", l2norm)
+    if hasattr(clip_grads, "multi_tensor_l2norm"):
+        rebound += rebind_everywhere(clip_grads, "multi_tensor_l2norm", l2norm)
+    mark_patched(clip_grads, _PATCH_KEY)
+    log_rank_0(f"[Patch:{_PATCH_KEY}] wrapped the l2norm in {', '.join(sorted(set(rebound)))}")
